name: WebCodecs (video and audio encode and decode)
plain: Gives direct access to the browser's video and audio codecs with no prompt.
meaning: A site can encode or decode media frames in code, often with hardware acceleration. Great for editors, but also lets a page probe which codecs and accelerators the device has.

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Available in workers; no iframe flag

limits.headline: Can open and make video and sound files by itself inside the page
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page plays, edits or records media.
can: Decode video and audio frame by frame
Make new video or audio files in the page
Use your device's chip to speed up video
cannot: Turn on your camera or microphone without a permission pop up
Go past what your device's chip can handle
Work on files it was not given
Run after you close the page

story.what_it_is: A page can use your device's video and sound chips directly to pack and unpack media.

marketing.name: WebCodecs
marketing.pitch: Chrome's docs say WebCodecs gives low level control over video and audio encoding and decoding in the browser.

story.for_you: You never see it. Web video editors, cloud games and calls just look sharper and use less battery, because the page uses hardware built for video.
story.for_makers: Makers get fast video processing without a plugin: custom players, editing, streaming with very low delay. It turns a tab into a serious media tool.

use_cases.example: Cloud gaming in a browser decodes the game video stream frame by frame with very little delay.
A web video editor cuts, exports and previews clips using hardware encoding.
A video call app packs your camera into small frames for the network.
A live streaming tool sends your webcam to viewers at very low delay.
A camera monitoring dashboard decodes many streams at once for a security guard.
A video ad player decodes ads with exact timing, so the ad counts as viewed.

technical_bounds: isConfigSupported() reveals codec and hardware support (fingerprint)
Hardware decoder instances are limited by the platform (a few at once on many devices)
Frames must be closed (VideoFrame.close()) or memory fills quickly
Safari support arrived at 16.4 for video; AudioEncoder later
No access to camera without getUserMedia
